stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A city has 1,600 bus stops, and 400 of them are in the downtown district. Planners chose 80 of the downtown stops at random and found that 30% of the stops they chose had a covered shelter.
choices: Approximately 30% of all bus stops in the city have a covered shelter.
Approximately 30% of bus stops in the downtown district have a covered shelter.
Approximately 70% of bus stops in the downtown district have a covered shelter.
Most of the bus stops in the downtown district have a covered shelter.
explanation: The planners only sampled downtown stops, so the 30% can only stand for the downtown district. Because the stops were chosen at random, you can carry the 30% over to all downtown stops, and you say 'approximately' because it is an estimate from a sample.

A.why: You applied the result to every stop in the city. No stops outside downtown were sampled, so the data say nothing about them.

C.why: 70% is the share of sampled stops that did NOT have a shelter. You reported the complement instead.

D.why: 30% is well under half, so the sample does not support a claim that most downtown stops have shelters.

stem: Which of the following is the most appropriate conclusion?
stimulus: A lake is home to painted turtles, snapping turtles, and musk turtles. Biologists captured a random sample of 150 painted turtles from the lake. Of the sampled painted turtles, 40% had a shell length greater than 15 centimeters.
choices: Approximately 40% of all turtles in the lake have a shell length greater than 15 centimeters.
The average painted turtle in the lake has a shell length greater than 15 centimeters.
Approximately 40% of painted turtles in the lake have a shell length greater than 15 centimeters.
Approximately 60% of painted turtles in the lake have a shell length greater than 15 centimeters.
explanation: Only painted turtles were sampled, so the result applies to painted turtles in this lake. You keep the same statistic (40% above 15 centimeters) and hedge it with 'approximately.'

A.why: You extended the result to every turtle species in the lake. Snapping turtles and musk turtles were never sampled.

B.why: You turned a percent above a threshold into a claim about the average. Since only 40% are above 15 centimeters, the data do not show that the average is above 15 centimeters.

D.why: 60% is the share of sampled painted turtles that were NOT longer than 15 centimeters. You attached the complement to the wrong condition.

stem: Which of the following conclusions is most appropriate?
stimulus: A marine biologist picked 200 blue rockfish at random from a coastal kelp forest and checked each one for parasites. Of these fish, 30% had parasites.
choices: Approximately 30% of all fish in the kelp forest have parasites.
Approximately 30% of blue rockfish in the kelp forest have parasites.
Most blue rockfish in the kelp forest have about 30 parasites.
Exactly 30% of blue rockfish in the kelp forest have parasites.
explanation: Only blue rockfish from this kelp forest were randomly sampled, so the sample can speak only for that group. You carry the same statistic, 30% with parasites, over to blue rockfish in the kelp forest and hedge it with "approximately," because a sample gives an estimate, not an exact value.

A.why: You extended the result to every fish in the kelp forest, but only blue rockfish were sampled. Other species could have very different parasite rates.

C.why: You turned a percent of fish into a count of parasites per fish and made a claim about most fish. The 30% is the share of fish that had any parasites, not how many parasites each fish carries.

D.why: You treated the sample percent as an exact population value. A random sample of 200 fish gives an estimate, so the conclusion needs to say "approximately."

stem: Which of the following conclusions is most appropriate?
stimulus: A nutrition researcher picked 150 adults at random from one city's registered vegetarians and recorded each person's daily iron intake. Of these adults, 40% took in less than the recommended amount of iron.
choices: The average vegetarian adult in the city takes in less than the recommended amount of iron.
Approximately 40% of all adults in the city take in less than the recommended amount of iron.
Approximately 40% of registered vegetarian adults in the city take in less than the recommended amount of iron.
Approximately 60% of registered vegetarian adults in the city take in less than the recommended amount of iron.
explanation: The random sample came only from the city's registered vegetarians, so the conclusion should be about that group. You keep the same statistic, 40% below the recommended amount, and hedge it with "approximately" because it comes from a sample.

A.why: You turned a percent below a threshold into a claim about the average. Since only 40% fell short, the data don't show that the average intake is below the recommended amount, and they suggest a majority met it.

B.why: You extended the result to all adults in the city, but only registered vegetarians were sampled. Adults who eat meat could have very different iron intake.

D.why: You used the complement. 60% is the share who met or went above the recommended amount, not the share who fell short.
